title: Manufacturer with IT/OT convergence

organisation.name: Ardent Forge Components
organisation.size: 1,700 staff across two plants; IT team of 25, two OT engineers
organisation.summary: Ardent Forge Components machines brake and steering parts on production lines run by PLCs and HMI panels. OT engineers program the PLCs from an engineering workstation that they reach over RDP through a jump host in the IT/OT DMZ; the jump host is joined to the corporate Active Directory. The plant historian replicates process data to a replica in the DMZ, from which a connector posts production counts to the cloud ERP. The line OEM supports its machines through a remote access portal, a passive OT monitoring sensor watches the plant network, and the SIEM collects EDR and AD logs.

network_security.summary: From a phished office PC through the DMZ jump host to the engineering workstation
The PLC cabinet's cellular modem is a way into the plant that skips the DMZ

endpoint_security.summary: The jump host and the engineering workstation run no EDR
A malicious attachment on an office PC steals the user's domain credentials

incident_response.summary: Ransomware on office PCs: should the IT/OT link be cut, and when?
The OT sensor reports a PLC program download nobody scheduled

security_operations.summary: OT sensor alerts reach the SIEM, but the SOC rota cannot triage them
A member is added to the OT-Remote group at night

threat_intelligence.summary: An advisory on a group that targets manufacturers' engineering workstations
A report that an OEM's remote support platform was breached

identity_access.summary: Corporate AD decides who reaches the plant network
ERP sign-in is federated with the same corporate AD

grc_risk.summary: No documented zones and conduits; the cellular modem is in no risk register
Engineering systems cannot be patched without the OEM's sign-off

zero_trust.summary: Reaching the jump host is treated as being trusted to reach the plant
The ERP trusts the DMZ connector's API key for any order change

cloud_security.summary: The ERP connector's API key can write purchase orders, not only production counts
A forged federation token signs in to the cloud ERP as a payroll admin

reviewNotes: Advanced: corporate AD gates OT access (subtle), and the cellular modem bypasses every IT/OT control (subtle). Present controls with limits: EDR not on the engineering systems, the OT sensor blind to the modem, one-way replication that is not one-way for its account.
